image_description: Two male mallard ducks (drakes) floating on green rippled water. The duck on the left is in profile facing right, showing a glossy iridescent green head, white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey body. The duck on the right is facing slightly towards the viewer/left, also displaying characteristic mallard plumage. Both are reflected in the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both ducks clearly display the characteristic broad, flat, yellow-green bills typical of male mallards.
Dark eyes are visible on both subjects, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bodies appear streamlined and sit low in the water, indicating buoyancy and correct aquatic adaptation. Plumage texture appears dense.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both subjects exhibit the specific breeding plumage of male mallards: iridescent green heads, distinct white neck rings, chestnut breasts, and grey flanks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ducks are floating on water; their legs and feet are submerged and completely occluded from view.
The folded wings on the sides of the bodies appear broad and taper correctly, consistent with avian anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck on the right clearly displays the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (drake feathers). The duck on the left shows a short tail consistent with the posture.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The water ripples have a slightly repetitive, 'painted' texture rather than natural fluid dynamics. Some ripple patterns near the reflections appear slightly inconsistent with the light source direction.
The reflections are somewhat soft and lack the precise distortion expected from the specific ripple shapes immediately beneath them, suggesting a slight generative smoothing artifact.
